why: The Enterprise Command Center was a SECOND product architecture: a page that
answered every question the rest of the product answers, from its own
computations, with its own vocabularies. This file assigns every one of its
sections a single final owner, so the page becomes a set of projections of
authorities that already exist rather than an authority of its own.
HOME        cockpit summary — 'what is the state of my workspace?'
OPERATIONS  shared unresolved work — 'what must we act on?'
SECURITY    security-specialised decisions, Security Center owned
DOMAIN      a specific domain surface already owns it
REMOVE      a true duplicate; deleted with its consumers
'projection' means the Command Center may RENDER it and must not COMPUTE
it: the numbers come from the owner's authority, and acting on them
happens on the owner's surface where the capability gates live.

accessSecurityAnomalies.note: A security decision. Operations may summarise and link; it must never adjudicate.

accessSecurityClassifier.note: Same. Classification of access risk stays Security-owned.

attentionQueue.note: Backward-compatible alias of operationalPressure.items. Kept only for shipped clients; carries no independent computation.

caseOperations.note: Case state belongs to the case domain; the Command Center summarises it.

coordinationSignals.note: Cross-operator coordination backlog. Shared, unresolved, and already owned.

crossCaseIntelligenceV2.note: Cross-case analysis, second generation. Analysis answers 'what does this mean?'; it is never a piece of shared work and it never resolves anything.

deepIntegrityWatch.note: Per-Evidence integrity FAILURES are Operations conditions (Phase 3). The WATCH surface — ongoing scrutiny of records not yet failing — stays Security.

governancePosture.note: A posture summary is cockpit material. Governance actions live on the governance surfaces.

incidents.note: Already a projection. Adjudication (acknowledge/assign/resolve/suppress) is capability-gated on /operations and never here.

operationalGraph.note: Despite the name this is a graph VISUALISATION, not an operations queue.

operationalPressure.note: WAS a second general Operations computation — a dozen bespoke scans with their own severity ranking and caps, reporting a workspace's operational pressure independently of /operations. Rewritten to project the canonical summary and the canonical condition list. This is the duplicate-pressure-authority removal the phase exists for.

organizationalHealth.note: Organisational health analytics for executives; distinct from the workspace Operations summary, which counts unresolved work.

organizationalIntelligence.note: Analysis, not operations. It answers 'what does this mean?', never 'what must we do?'.

organizationalIntelligenceV2.note: Versioned variant of the above; same destination and same authority.

pipeline.note: The compact pipeline counters. Cockpit material — the same numbers Home already renders, from the same projection.

pipelineDetail.note: The cockpit pipeline view Home already consumes.

pipelineIntelligence.note: Predictive and comparative reading of pipeline throughput. Advisory only: it never opens, escalates or resolves a condition.

predictiveRisk.note: A prediction is advisory. It is never an operational condition, and it never resolves anything.

queueCongestion.note: BullMQ depth is PROOVRA infrastructure telemetry, not a tenant's work.

queueWorkerTelemetry.note: Worker liveness is platform health. A tenant cannot act on it.

relationshipIntelligence.note: Entity relationships are an analytical product.

reviewerCapacity.note: Capacity planning is a reviewer-ops surface.

reviewerOrchestration.note: Review has its own lifecycle and must not acquire a second one.

reviewerWorkload.note: Who is carrying how much review work. Operator workload is an Operations concern; the reviewer-ops engine stays its authority and its assignment lifecycle.

routingQueue.note: Routing is operational work assignment; the workflow authority owns its lifecycle.

summary.note: A cockpit header. Counts only; no lifecycle, no actions.

timelineIntelligence.note: Analytical reading of the timeline, as distinct from the timeline itself. Analysis surface, not an operations queue.

workloadEngine.note: Operator workload is an Operations concern; the reviewer-ops engine remains the authority.
